sentences.text:
Heard Ms. Namrata K. Agrawal, learned counsel for applicant/accused and Mr. Madhur Shukla,
learned standing counsel for EOW on the question of admission as well final disposal.
4. Facts suffice to decide the present petition in brief are that, Crime No.32/2022 under Section 409, 420, 120-B of IPC and 13(1)(b) r/w 13(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 was registered against the present applicant and other accused persons and after investigation, EOW submitted charge sheet before the Special Court.

During investigation, transaction in the Bank Account No.1411101022205 maintained with Canara Bank Branch Rewa and two FDR's No.876293 and 876286 were freeze by the investigating agency, upon the allegations that the misappropriated amount was transferred in the said accounts.

Applicant/accused preferred an application under Section 451/457 of Cr.P.C. for permitting the applicant to operate the bank account and withdraw the amount of the FDR's, which was dismissed by the impugned order dated 27.5.2023.

Impugned order is assailed by the learned counsel for application mainly on the ground that investigating agency attached the bank account in exercise of powers under Section 102 of Cr.P.C., which is not permissible and learned Special Judge failed to consider that bank account cannot be freezed by any investigating agency under Section 102 of Cr.P.C. as Section 18(A) of Prevention of Corruption Act,
provides separate procedure for the same.

5. Learned counsel relied on the order passed by the Apex Court in the matter of Ratan Babula Loth vs. State of Karnataka, 2021 SC OnLine 875, wherein the Apex Court set aside the order of freezing of the account and granted liberty to the investigating agency to take such recourse in law as may be permissible.

entities.text: Ratan Babula Loth vs. State of Karnataka, 2021 SC OnLine 875
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Judgment passed in the matter of Octo Circuit Limited vs. Axis Bank and another,
(2021 6 SCC 707 is also relied by the counsel for the petitioner wherein dealing with the case of Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, Apex Court held that freezing of bank account under PMLA Act is permissible but it cannot be freezed by exercising the power under Section 102 of Cr.P.C.
6.

entities.text:
Octo Circuit Limited vs. Axis Bank and another,
(2021 6 SCC 707
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for applicant prays for setting aside the impugned order and passed suitable direction to permit the applicant to operate the aforesaid Bank Account and withdraw the amount of FDR's.
7 .

Per contra, learned counsel appearing for Investigating Agency supported the order passed by the Special Judge mainly on the ground that huge amount was embezzled and misappropriated amount of money was transferred in the bank account.

The applicant earlier also moved an application under Sections 451/457 of Cr.P.C. which was dismissed by order dated 28.10.2022 and the same was not challenged, therefore, the Special Judge has not committed any error in dismissing the present application.

During the pendency of present petition, Investigating Agency on 4.8.2023 moved an application under Section 3 of Criminal Law (Amendment) Ordinance, 1944 and Section 5(6), 18 (A)(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act for the purpose of attaching the bank account and money lying therein.

He placed the copy of application on record with a prayer that as the application has already been moved to attach the money, no permission can be granted to operate Bank Account and withdraw the amount of FDR's.
8. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

sentences.text: By perusal of the record it appears that amount of Rs.53.00 lacs (Approx.) were transferred in the Bank Account maintained with Canara Bank, which was as per the prosecution opened for the purpose of siphoning the money.
Other co-accused persons were also opened the bank account in Canara Bank for the same purpose.
After investigation charge sheet has already been filed.
The trial is going on.

It appears from the impugned order that earlier the petitioner preferred an application registered as MJCR No.2408/2022 for the same relief, which was dismissed by Special Judge on 28.10.2022 and without assailing the order of dismissal of earlier application, second application was moved by petitioner for the same relief, without disclosing the filing of earlier application and change in the circumstance.
Learned Special Judge by the impugned order, dismissed the application mainly on the ground that earlier also the application was moved and dismissed.
The reason for dismissal of the application preferred by petitioner by impugned order appears to be legal and justified.
If any order has already been passed by a criminal court, the criminal court has no jurisdiction to differ with the earlier order on subsequent stage, without any change in circumstances.

10. In the present matter, it is not the case of petitioner that after dismissal of earlier application,
there were some material changes in the circumstances of the case and, therefore, the order impugned does not require any interference.
The petitioner has not challenged the earlier order passed on 28.10.2022.

However, considering the fact that investigating agency has already moved an application under Section 3 of Criminal Law (Amendment) Ordinance, 1944 r/w Section 5(6),
18(A)(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act, the liberty is granted to the petitioner to raise all available grounds before the Special Court at the time of hearing of the aforesaid application and Special Judge will decide the aforesaid application of the investigating agency without influenced by the order passed by Special Judge on 28.10.2022 and 27.5.2023.
11. With the aforesaid, present petition is dismissed.
No order as to costs.

(SHEEL NAGU) (
 JUDGE   irfan Dr. S.U. Khan @ Shami Ullah Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36811693/
